public_rationale: The 2009 study recovered geographic relationships from newspaper text. The 2017 paper evaluated geographic positions recovered from older word embeddings. These establish Marcus's narrow historical point: approximate geographic information had already been recovered from language corpora.
limitations: This does not establish that the 2023 paper lacked other novel contributions or achieved no improvement.
The 2009 availability date is conservatively represented by the end of its documented publication month; the accessible record does not establish the exact day.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The finding that geography can be inferred from language corpora is not new; earlier work from 2009 and 2017 showed similar results.

statement.excerpt: It’s also not even remotely new.

from_speaker: geography can be weakly but imperfectly inferred from language corpora
earlier results that are essentially similar
our_interpretation: The claim concerns the earlier discovery of geographic information in text-derived representations, not whether every contribution of the 2023 paper lacked novelty.
Similar results means recovering approximate geographic locations or spatial relationships from language corpora. Identical models, datasets and accuracy are not required.
criteria.support_condition: The named earlier research demonstrates approximate geographic recovery from text-derived representations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The earlier studies do not recover geographic information from language corpora, or their relevant findings first appeared after the 2023 paper.

evidence.publisher: Cognitive Science; abstract reproduced by PubMed
evidence.explanation: Louwerse and Zwaan recovered geographic relationships among 50 US cities using newspaper text, latent semantic analysis and multidimensional scaling. This directly establishes the earlier finding Marcus describes.

evidence.publisher: Asian Federation of Natural Language Processing / ACL Anthology
evidence.explanation: Konkol and colleagues evaluated geographic positions recoverable through linear transformations of older word embeddings. This establishes a comparable research task years before the 2023 paper.
